title: Consumers turn to buy now, pay later for daily essentials | KTVU
summary: KTVU interview with a Financial Technology Association spokesperson presents BNPL's growth and repayment statistics from the industry's own perspective.

assertions.quote: more Americans are using the short term loans to pay for everyday necessities groceries, rent, medical bills, car repairs.
96% of buy now, pay later pay in for loans are paid in full and on time

verdicts.note: Company-reported on-time rates are high and plausible for the median loan, but independent surveys find a substantial minority (roughly a third to half) report at least one problem, so 'most... do not report serious problems' holds only loosely.
Fed SHED finds about 74% of BNPL users were not late on any payment in the prior year, consistent with most use going smoothly.
CFPB: only 3.8% of borrowers had a loan charged off in 2021 (up from 2.9% in 2020), consistent with the large majority of BNPL loans being paid back.

assertions.quote: which, you know, comes with no, no debt really, or no compounding interest on the plan

verdicts.note: Accurately describes the marketing pitch; whether it is actually safer depends on usage patterns the marketing doesn't control for.

CFPB: unlike credit-card interest (which compounds and cost Americans roughly $120 billion a year), BNPL late fees 'do not compound,' and borrowers who miss payments 'may be prohibited from future use until they repay' rather than continuing to accrue interest.

assertions.quote: providers will allow you to reschedule up to a certain number of times a month payment dates
